questions.question: Under which article of the Indian Constitution, the President can declare a state of national emergency?
questions.explanation: Article 352 allows the President to declare a national emergency.

questions.question: Which of the following is a basic feature of the Indian Constitution?
questions.explanation: Federalism is a basic feature of the Indian Constitution.

questions.question: Who is the head of the West Bengal Legislative Assembly?
questions.explanation: The Chief Minister is the head of the West Bengal Legislative Assembly.

questions.question: What is the name of the highest court in the state of West Bengal?
questions.explanation: The Calcutta High Court is the highest court in the state of West Bengal.

questions.question: Which of the following is a fundamental right under the Indian Constitution?
questions.explanation: Right to Life is a fundamental right under the Indian Constitution.

questions.question: The first session of the Indian National Congress was held in 1885 in?
questions.explanation: It was held in Calcutta.

questions.question: Who was the president of the Indian National Congress when the Non-Cooperation Movement was launched in 1920?
questions.explanation: Mahatma Gandhi was the president.

questions.explanation: The Regulating Act was passed.

questions.explanation: Bengal Volunteers was formed.

questions.question: Who was the leader of the Swadeshi movement in Bengal in the early 20th century?
questions.explanation: Aurobindo Ghosh was the leader.

questions.explanation: The agreement was to develop NH 2 between Dankuni and Asansol.

questions.question: The West Bengal government launched which scheme to provide financial assistance to the women affected by cyclones in the state?
questions.explanation: The Bhagya Lakshmi Yojana provides financial assistance to women affected by cyclones.

questions.explanation: The Adi Ganga Riverfront development project is a major focus of the government.

questions.explanation: The West Bengal E-Mobility Policy aims to promote the use of electric vehicles in the state.

questions.question: The Government of West Bengal has set a target to increase the use of renewable energy to what percentage of the state's total energy consumption by 2028?
questions.explanation: The state aims to increase renewable energy usage to 50% of total energy consumption by 2028.

questions.explanation: It benefits students of classes 1 to 12.

questions.explanation: It provides financial assistance to farmers.

options: Department of Health and Family Welfare

questions.question: The Unnayan project is a scheme of the Government of West Bengal for which category of people?
questions.explanation: It aims to improve the living conditions of the urban poor.

questions.question: The Rupashree Prakalpa is a scheme of which West Bengal government department for the welfare of married women?
options: Department of Women and Child Development
Department of Health and Family Welfare

questions.question: A shopkeeper in Kolkata sells an article at a profit of 15% and makes a gain of ₹ 45. If the cost price of the article is ₹ 300, what is the selling price of the article?
questions.explanation: Profit is calculated as cost price * profit percentage.

questions.question: A person purchases a plot of land in West Bengal for ₹ 8 lakhs at a discount of 5% and sells it for ₹ 12 lakhs. What is the percentage of profit made by the person?
questions.explanation: Profit percentage is calculated as (selling price - cost price) / cost price * 100.

questions.question: A man buys 15 kg of potatoes in Howrah at the rate of ₹ 20 per kg and sells them in Burdwan at the rate of ₹ 25 per kg. What is his percentage profit?
questions.explanation: Profit percentage is calculated as (selling price - cost price) / cost price * 100.

questions.question: A person buys a share in a company at ₹ 80 and it rises to ₹ 120 in the market. If he sells the share at this price, what is his percentage profit?
questions.explanation: Profit percentage is calculated as (selling price - cost price) / cost price * 100.

questions.question: A dealer in a shop at Sealdah sells an article at a loss of 8% and makes a loss of ₹ 24. If the cost price of the article is ₹ 360, what is the selling price of the article?
questions.explanation: Loss is calculated as cost price * loss percentage.

questions.question: A person can finish 1/4th of a piece of work in 3 hours. How many hours will he take to finish the whole work?
questions.explanation: Work done in 3 hours is 1/4, so total work will be done in 12 hours.

questions.question: A tap can fill 1/3rd of a tank in 2 hours. Another tap can fill 1/4th of the tank in 3 hours. If both taps are opened simultaneously, how long will it take to fill the tank?
questions.explanation: Combined rate of filling the tank is 1/3 + 1/4 = 7/12 per hour, so tank will be filled in 12/7 hours.

questions.question: A pipe can fill 1/6th of a canal in 10 hours. In how many hours will it fill the entire canal if 2 more pipes, each filling 1/8th of the canal in 12 hours, are added?
questions.explanation: Combined rate of filling the canal is 1/6 + 2*(1/8) = 7/24 per hour, so canal will be filled in 24/7 hours.

questions.question: A person can do a piece of work in 8 hours. He works for 3 hours a day. How many days will he take to complete the work?
questions.explanation: Work done in 3 hours a day is 3/8, so total work will be done in 6 days.

questions.question: A pipe can fill 2/3rd of a tank in 3 hours. How many hours will it take to fill 1/4th of the tank?
questions.explanation: Rate of filling the tank is 2/3 per 3 hours, i.e., 2/9 per hour, so 1/4th of the tank will be filled in 3/2 hours.

questions.question: Kajal is the daughter of Shubho and his wife. If Shubho's wife is the sister of Bipasha, then how is Bipasha related to Kajal?
questions.explanation: Bipasha is Kajal's aunt.

questions.question: If Raju is the brother of Gopal and the son of Durga, then what is the relationship between Durga and Gopal?
questions.explanation: Durga is Gopal's father.

questions.question: Bibhas is the grandson of a man whose father is the only son of a certain woman. How is Bibhas related to this woman?
questions.explanation: Bibhas is the woman's grandson.

questions.explanation: Priya's mother is the woman's grandmother.

questions.question: A man's mother is the only sister of his father-in-law. If the man's son is called Soumen, then how is Soumen related to the man's father-in-law?
questions.explanation: Soumen is the man's father-in-law's grandson.

questions.question: A person starts walking from a place where the sun is at his back. He walks 6 km due east and then 4 km due north. He then walks 3 km due south. Which direction is he facing now?
questions.explanation: He would be facing west after walking south.

questions.question: A person is standing at a point A on the banks of a river. He sees a temple at a distance of 5 km on the opposite bank. He knows that he has to walk 10 km east to reach a point B on the same bank, where he can take a ferry to cross the river. How far is the temple from point B?
questions.explanation: The temple is at the same distance from point B as it is from point A.

questions.question: A person walks 8 km due north from his home. He then walks 10 km due east. Finally, he walks 6 km due south. How far is he from home now?
questions.explanation: He is 6 km away from home due to the 6 km walk south.

questions.question: A man is facing a fort. In front of him, there is a road that leads to the fort. To his right, there is a tree, and to his left, there is a pond. Which direction is the man facing?
questions.explanation: He is facing east because the road is in front of him.

questions.question: A person walks 12 km due west. Then, he walks 8 km south. Then, he walks 6 km west. Finally, he walks 5 km north. How far is he from his starting point?
questions.explanation: He is 10 km away from his starting point.
